topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the focus on integrating previously taught immune system components involved in initiating and resolving inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects pathogens and cellular damage through molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptor families, and downstream signaling pathways.

topics.label: Inflammatory response propagation, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells initiate local leukocyte recruitment, promote lymphatic trafficking for adaptive immunity, and can lead to severe systemic conditions like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue repair, and lead to chronic inflammatory states and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the subject of the next lecture.
